newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Mobil sets $1.6 billion venture with Venezuela firm.
newsitem.headline: Mobil sets $1.6 billion venture with Venezuela firm.

text.p: Mobil Chemical Co. Thursday signed a $1.6 billion joint venture deal with Pequiven, part of the state-run Petroleos de Venezuela oil company, to develop a series of petrochemical plants.
The tentative agreement was signed by Mobil Corp. Executive Vice President Eugene Renna and Pequiven President Arnold Volkenborn at a public ceremony.
A 50-50 joint venture company will be formed by the end of the year to operate the facility and market its products. The complex is expected to start operations in the year 2000.
The complex at Jose, a seashore existing petrochemicals site in eastern Anzoategui state, is expected to create about 4,600 construction jobs and 600 new permanent operations jobs in the area.
The petrochemicals complex will ultimately be one of the biggest in the world, with one olefins plant, two polyethylene plants and one glycol plant producing plastics and their raw materials.
Mobil's stock rose $2.25 to $128.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
